title: Batch, flex and async
summary: Batch and Flex processing trade time for a 50% lower price. Batch queues a file for a 24-hour target, and Flex keeps a synchronous API shape but can be preempted.
useIf: Nobody waits for the result: evaluations, enrichment, embeddings, classification, backfills.
avoidIf: A user is waiting, or you cannot tolerate 429, 408 or a result hours later.

explain.md: **Batch** takes a file of requests and returns results later. Azure Global Batch and Data Zone Batch cost 50% less than Global Standard, aim to finish within 24 hours, use a separate enqueued-token quota and carry no real-time SLA [[r5]]. OpenAI's Batch API is also 50% off with its own higher limits and a 24-hour window; the input is a `.jsonl` file with a unique `custom_id` per line, one model per file, up to 200 MB, and the queue counts as pending input tokens [[r12]]. Anthropic Message Batches take up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB, most finish within an hour, and they expire after 24 hours with results kept 29 days [[r13]].

**Flex** is a per-request tier: set `service_tier: "flex"`. On Azure it is a preview for Global Standard at 50% off, with cached-token discounts, no latency or service SLA and preemptible capacity, so a 429 can mean no capacity and a 408 means raise the client timeout (doc samples use 900 seconds). There is no automatic fallback to Standard, it shares quota with Standard, and from 2026-09-25 unsupported models return 400 [[r11]]. OpenAI lists Flex as a beta at Batch API rates, with prompt-caching discounts on top, and its example raises the client timeout to 15 minutes [[tr9]].

pitfalls.symptom: A Flex job loses interactive capacity
pitfalls.cause: Flex shares quota with Standard, so a surge consumes the same allowance
pitfalls.fix: Cap Flex concurrency, run it off-peak, or use a separate deployment

pitfalls.symptom: Flex calls fail with 429 even at low volume
pitfalls.cause: Capacity is preemptible and there is no automatic fallback
pitfalls.fix: Retry with backoff, then fall back to Standard in your own code

pitfalls.symptom: Batch finished but outputs do not match inputs
pitfalls.cause: Results return in no guaranteed order
pitfalls.fix: Key every request with a unique `custom_id` and join on it; replay only failed ids

quiz.q: Order these by how long the caller can wait, shortest first.
quiz.explain: Interactive tiers serve people waiting. Flex fits minutes of slack and tolerates preemption. Batch fits hours with a 24-hour target [[r5]].

quiz.q: Flex calls on Azure return 408. What does the doc advise?
options: Raise the client timeout; samples use 900 seconds
quiz.explain: On Azure Flex a 408 means raise the timeout, while a 429 can mean no capacity [[r11]]. PTU is unrelated, and immediate retries add load.

quiz.q: Which are true of the OpenAI Batch API?
quiz.explain: The guide describes a 50% discount, one model per file and unique `custom_id` values. Ordering is not guaranteed, which is why `custom_id` exists [[r12]].

flashcards.front: What do Batch and Flex give and take?
flashcards.back: About 50% off in exchange for time. Batch has a 24-hour target. Flex is synchronous but preemptible with no SLA.
It shares quota with Standard and has no automatic fallback, so a surge or a 429 needs your own handling.
Results are not guaranteed to return in input order. The id joins outputs to inputs and drives replay of failures.
